- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.6) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.4) or volatile, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction to pessimism.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in the following 5–10 days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% to prevent overcorrection.
- Model shows persistent lag in mean reversion: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast often stays above; if below, it lags below — adjust forecast to closer match 30-day MA.
- In high-sentiment environments (sentiment > 0.7), forecast tends to be too conservative; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to reflect sentiment-driven momentum.
- In low-sentiment environments (sentiment < 0.3), forecast often overestimates recovery; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to reflect subdued market behavior.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a dip, model often fails to capture the full rebound; add a 1–2% upward bias in the next 3–5 days.
